title: About Evaluated Applications
description: An independent AI research lab in England. What it builds, how the results are reported, and where to find them.
headline: About
lede: Evaluated Applications is an independent AI research lab in England. It builds the parts most AI work takes for granted, and publishes them as .NET libraries you can install and run.

sections.title: What is built
items: **Phasor** holds the Pleroma: one fixed-size array of exact integers that answers fifty different questions in a single pass over it.
**AlgFormer**: a population of small holographic language models that talk through one shared wave, in plain C#.
**HoloDb**: an embedded SQL database that learns from the queries it serves and keeps only what pays.
**EvalApp**: the pipeline runner that spreads work across the cores you have.
Prose, Tracer, HoloGenome, HoloVoxel and Blazier, each one library with one job.
paragraphs: All of them are on [Products](/products/). Several run in a browser tab under [Tools](/tools/).

sections.title: How results are reported
paragraphs: Every number is published with the conditions it was measured in. The places where the work lost are listed beside the places where it won, on the [Evidence](/evidence/) pages. When a claim stops being true, the page changes. The pages describe what the code does today and nothing else.

sections.title: Licence
paragraphs: The software is proprietary. Evaluation and non-commercial development or testing are permitted. Commercial, production or revenue-generating use needs a commercial licence from the owner. Terms are on the [Licence](/licence/) page.

sections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Partnership and licence enquiries: [Partner with us](/partner/). Automated readers: [For agents](/ai/).
